title: Brazil-Chile Bilateral Joint Declaration Violations — State Failure to Implement Diplomatic Human Rights Commitments from August 5-6, 2024 Presidential Summit
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law
allegation_summary: On August 5-6, 2024 — exactly one month after the LA8159 incident — the Presidents of Brazil (Lula da Silva) and Chile (Gabriel Boric) signed a Joint Presidential Declaration containing 58 bilateral agreement points covering human rights, consular cooperation, citizen protection, and aviation cooperation. This declaration, signed while the passenger's case was actively being processed by both countries' regulatory bodies, established binding diplomatic commitments that were subsequently violated by ANAC (Brazil) and DGAC (Chile) in their handling of the LA8159 complaint. Key commitments breached include: human rights protection for citizens of both countries, consular cooperation and assistance, and citizen access to justice and administrative remedies. The declaration represents a binding diplomatic instrument under international law (VCLT Art. 26 — pacta sunt servanda).

candidate_articles.history_note: DOCTRINAL WEAKNESS: Joint Presidential Declarations are POLITICAL COMMITMENTS, not binding treaties under VCLT. Same issue as BR-015. VCLT Art. 26 applies to 'treaties' as defined in VCLT Art. 2(1)(a). Joint Declarations generally do not meet the VCLT criteria for a 'treaty' unless they demonstrate an intention to create legal (not just political) obligations. The file presents the Joint Declaration as if it were a treaty binding under pacta sunt servanda — this is doctrinally inaccurate.
